Summary written 2026-10-17. The an agent branch
claude/modest-cannon-kols9r
was not on origin, so this records the reported findings from that search.
Finding
There is
no public machine-readable citywide designation layer
for UHOP Schedule E-1 (Urban Land Use Designations) or RHOP Schedule D (Rural Land Use Designations).
The City's internal GIS server (
itvpgisappint.hamilton.ca
) is not reachable from outside.
Searched: 1,697 public layers, 594 ArcGIS Online services, McMaster, Mohawk, Waterloo, Hamilton Conservation Authority and Ontario GeoHub.
Usable now
Secondary Plan Land Use

— URL: https://spatialsolutions.hamilton.ca/webgis/rest/services/General/PolicyPlanning/MapServer/6 · Notes: 47,212 lot-cut polygons, 31 plans, 67 classes, last amended 2026-05-12. Filter out four retired plans. Plan names don't match the secondary plan boundary layer. Not on open.hamilton.ca. No licence stated (not a gate per HARD-RULES 6; record it for provenance).
PolicyPlanning MapServer (service)
— URL: https://spatialsolutions.hamilton.ca/webgis/rest/services/General/PolicyPlanning/MapServer · Notes: Parent service; layers catalogued separately.
Employment Lands
— URL: Employment_Lands/FeatureServer/2 (open.hamilton.ca) · Notes: 22 polygons, derived from Schedule E-1 employment designations.
Provincial overlays
— URL: LIO · Notes: Niagara Escarpment Plan, Greenbelt Plan, 2019 Provincially Significant Employment Zones.
All three Hamilton rows are in the catalog (merged in PR #62).
Fallback for the citywide designation
Ask the City for the internal E-1 / D designation layer.
Vector-extract the schedule PDFs. They are vector CorelDRAW exports, so polygons can be pulled out and georeferenced. Estimate: about 6–7 person-days.
The schedule PDFs carry a Teranet copyright notice. Under HARD-RULES 6 (licences don't gate) this doesn't block use, but record it for provenance.
